title: ALMAGAL: VI. The spatial distribution of dense cores during the evolution of cluster-forming massive clumps
question: Characterize where and how dense cores are distributed in massive potentially cluster-forming clumps to trace how fragmentation is initially set and proceeds across early evolutionary stages before gas dispersal.

data.sensitivity: ~0.05 mJy/beam in the central region of the FoV

what.value: ALMAGAL compact source/core catalog (positions, sizes, densities, and masses of 6348 objects in 844 clumps)

evidence.loc: ALMAGAL core catalog
evidence.quote: (cite: Coletta2025) extracted compact sources in ALMAGAL continuum images using a modified version of the CuTEx photometric package (cite: Molinari2011). The entire catalog of identified compact sources is composed of 6348 objects detected at 5$\sigma$ in 844 clumps.

evidence.loc: ALMAGAL core catalog
evidence.quote: We adopted the positions provided by (cite: Coletta2025) to analyze how the cores are distributed in the fields and to measure their relative separations

evidence.loc: Mass segregation in the ALMAGAL fields
evidence.quote: We adopted the core masses estimated from (cite: Coletta2025) and computed $\Lambda_{MSR}(N_{MST})$ in the 296 ALMAGAL fields hosting at least eight cores

what.value: Updated ALMAGAL clump physical properties (heliocentric distances, masses, luminosities, surface densities, dust temperatures)

evidence.loc: The ALMAGAL clump sample
evidence.quote: The ALMAGAL clumps, with physical properties updated thanks to these new measurements, have masses $M$ between $\sim100$ and 12000 M$_{\odot}$, bolometric luminosity, $L$, between $\sim50$ and $\sim5\times10^{5}$ L$_{\odot}$, and are located in the Galaxy at heliocentric distances, $d_{cl}$, from $\sim1$ up to 14 kpc

evidence.loc: The Jeans length and mass for ALMAGAL clumps
evidence.quote: adopting as temperature the one of the dust, $T_{d}$, derived from Herschel/Hi-GAL data and reported in Table A.1 in (cite: Molinari2025).

external_data.citation: (cite: Molinari2025; Elia2025arXiv); Benedettini et al. in prep.

what.value: Herschel Hi-GAL clump sizes (R_cl) and 250 um photometric centers

evidence.loc: Center and size of the clusters of ALMAGAL cores
evidence.quote: For this reason, we adopted the clump sizes, $R_{cl}$, determined from Herschel 250 $\mu$m data and defined as the circularized half-width at half-maximum of the elliptical Gaussian fit with CuTEx (cite: Molinari2016; Elia2021).

what.value: Core separations, Q parameters, and mass segregation measurements from the ASHES, CORE, ASSEMBLE, DIHCA, and SQUALO surveys for comparison

evidence.loc: Correlation with the clump evolution
evidence.quote: allow us to also compare our results with those of the surveys ASHES (cite: Sanhueza2019), CORE (cite: Beuther2018), and ASSEMBLE (cite: Xu2024), each of which observed systems in a specific evolutionary phase.

evidence.loc: Correlation with the clump evolution
evidence.quote: Only a few clumps with $1\,<\,L/M\,<\,10$ L$_{\odot}/$M$_{\odot}$ were observed before ALMAGAL, a large fraction of them were obtained by the SQUALO (cite: Traficante2023) and the DIHCA survey (cite: Ishihara2024).

recipe.goal: Select clump and core subsamples from the ALMAGAL catalog
recipe.method: Select ALMAGAL clumps hosting at least N_core >= 4 (514 clumps, 5728 cores) from the Coletta et al. (2025) catalog, further dividing into near (C2+C5) and far (C3+C6) groups and applying higher cuts (N_core >= 8 for mass segregation, N_core >= 10 for Q parameter).
key_parameters: N_cores >= 4 (514 clumps), N_cores >= 8 (296 clumps), N_cores >= 10 (226 clumps)
assumptions: All compact sources in the ALMAGAL catalog represent star-forming cores

recipe.goal: Determine cluster centers, sizes, convex hulls, and morphological elongations
recipe.method: Compute cluster center via geometrical and mass-weighted average of core positions; define cluster radius R_cluster as distance of farthest core from center; construct convex hull (CH) polygon of core positions; classify systems by comparing number of hull vertices N_v^hull to interior cores N_in^hull; measure elongation via ellipse fit to CH (e_CH, PA_CH) and ratio xi = R_cluster / R^CH.
key_parameters: Distance cut d_cl >= 3.7 kpc (347 clumps) and 3.7 <= d_cl <= 6.5 kpc (302 clumps) to test FoV bias on R_cluster^ph
assumptions: Compute R^CH without the 1/(1 - N_v^hull / N_cores) normalization factor due to small N_cores

recipe.goal: Compute minimum spanning tree (MST) core separations and deproject to 3D
recipe.method: Compute pairwise angular distance matrix delta(i,j) and extract the (N-1) MST edges l_i using an IDL implementation of Prim's algorithm; convert to linear projected separations using updated heliocentric distances; statistically deproject to 3D separations l_i^depr by multiplying by 4/pi; compute clump-averaged estimators (min, max, mean, median, 25th/75th percentiles, and Gaussian KDE mode and 68% peak width for 437 clumps with >5 cores).
key_parameters: Clump-averaged KDE mode computed for 437 clumps hosting > 5 cores
assumptions: Random 3D orientation of core pairs along the line of sight yielding an expected projection factor of pi/4

recipe.goal: Evaluate evolutionary and density trends of core separations
recipe.method: Compare stacked ensemble and clump-averaged deprojected separations across clump L/M evolutionary classes (L/M <= 1, 1 <= L/M <= 10, L/M >= 10 L_sun/M_sun) and as continuous functions of L/M, clump surface density Sigma_cl, and volume density n_cl; apply KS, Mann-Whitney U, Spearman, Pearson, and Silverman multimodality tests; fit power-law relations against Sigma_cl and n_cl.
key_parameters: L/M classes: L/M <= 1 (129 clumps), 1 <= L/M <= 10 (176 clumps), L/M >= 10 L_sun/M_sun (209 clumps)
assumptions: Spherical clump geometry and mean molecular weight per free particle mu = 2.37 (solar composition) to compute Sigma_cl and n_cl
Clump bolometric luminosity-to-mass ratio L/M is an indicator of evolutionary stage

recipe.goal: Compare observed core separations and masses with thermal Jeans fragmentation predictions
recipe.method: Compute clump-averaged thermal Jeans length lambda_J^th and thermal Jeans mass M_J^th from clump volume density n_cl and Herschel dust temperature T_d; compare clump-averaged (l^median, l^mode) and ensemble deprojected separations l^depr to lambda_J^th, and core masses M_core to M_J^th, across L/M and Sigma_cl.
assumptions: Non-magnetized, homogeneous, isothermal, and self-gravitating clump with gas and dust thermally coupled (T_g = T_d)

recipe.goal: Quantify spatial clustering structure using the Q parameter and calibrate with synthetic clusters
recipe.method: Compute the Cartwright & Whitworth (2004) Q = m_bar / s_bar parameter for ALMAGAL clumps; run 1.1 million 3D synthetic cluster realizations (radial power-law p = 0, 1, 2, 2.9 and fractal box-method D = 1.5, 2.0, 2.5 for N_cores = 4 to 30, projected to 2D) to calibrate Q thresholds for small N_cores; evaluate Q vs L/M for the 226 clumps with N_cores >= 10.
key_parameters: N_cores >= 10 (226 clumps); calibrated thresholds: Q < 0.65 (robustly subclustered), Q > 0.8 (robustly centrally concentrated), Q = 0.75 (approximate boundary for uniform distribution)
assumptions: 3D spherical radial power-law or 3D fractal box-method spatial distributions projected onto 2D plane

recipe.goal: Measure mass segregation using the Mass Segregation Ratio (Lambda_MSR) and Monte Carlo mass uncertainties
recipe.method: For the 296 clumps with N_cores >= 8, compute Lambda_MSR(N_MST) = <l_random> / l_M using 1000 random draws for <l_random>; propagate 20% Gaussian core mass uncertainties via 500 Monte Carlo realizations per clump; classify a clump as robustly mass segregated if Lambda_MSR exceeds unity by more than sigma_l,random in >70% of MC realizations; compute Mass Segregation Integral (MSI), Lambda_MSR^max, and N_MST^crit across L/M classes.
key_parameters: N_cores >= 8 (296 clumps); 1000 random draws for <l_random>; 500 Monte Carlo realizations with 20% Gaussian core mass uncertainty; >70% probability threshold for robust MS

score_reason: The paper operates entirely on well-defined catalog positions and masses from Coletta et al. (2025) and clump parameters from Molinari et al. (2025), provides explicit mathematical formulas for all spatial metrics (MST, deprojection, Jeans length/mass, Q, Lambda_MSR, MSI) and synthetic cluster generation, and releases the full output tables at CDS. Minor deductions for unstated KDE bandwidths and ellipse-fitting details.
rediscovery_reason: Given the published ALMAGAL core catalog (Coletta et al. 2025) and clump catalog (Molinari et al. 2025), all spatial metrics (MST separations, convex hull elongations, Q parameters, Lambda_MSR mass segregation ratios, and Jeans comparisons) can be directly and quantitatively reproduced from catalog tables alone.
